Hey Jordan great to meet you on the call. Quick post-call recap and the materials we discussed attached.

Post-call recap (TL;DR):
- Primary ask: Best first-pass configuration to balance grounding and cost for your legal+product KB.
- Short recommendation: Start with a medium-sized open-model for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) + separate lightweight reranker. Move to a stronger generator only where higher-quality is required (e.g., legal).

Attached (see files):
- acme_prompt_set_v1.json  prompt templates and eval prompts we suggest for your use cases.
- acme_benchmark_results.pdf  initial benchmark results from a simulated run on a subset of your corpus (10k docs).
- reranker_options.xlsx  oscillator of reranker choices we recommend and rough cost/latency numbers.

Model recommendations (starting point):
1) Retrieval embeddings: text-embedding-ada-002-equivalent (dense) for broad recall; if you need higher semantic sensitivity, we recommend trying a larger embedding model in a targeted eval.
2) Generator: MetaLlama-2-13B-Chat (quantization-aware) as the default for balance of quality/cost. For higher-stakes legal responses, use MetaLlama-2-70B-Chat (or a hosted higher-accuracy variant) gated behind a policy for escalation.
3) Reranker: start with a lightweight cross-encoder reranker (DistilCross-768) for production pilot. If grounding is still low, evaluate a stronger cross-encoder (Cross-encoder-large) on the eval set.

Retrieval settings to try (pilot):
- Embedding model: text-embedding-ada-002-equivalent
- Vector DB: Faiss or Milvus with HNSW index
- Candidate pool: 200
- Rerank top-K: 20
- Similarity threshold (post-rerank): score >= 0.45 to surface as grounded; tune per vertical.

Quality/regression notes:
- Quantized generator variants can introduce subtle verbatim-matter regressions (~1-3% drop in MRR on legal prompts in our tests). We recommend running a focused regression eval (we included prompt sets) before switching fleet-wide.
- Reranker choice has outsized impact on grounding precision; moving from a bi-encoder only flow to a cross-encoder reranker improved precision@1 by ~12 points in our simulated runs.

Next steps & asks:
1) We ran a quick subset benchmark; see acme_benchmark_results.pdf. Can you confirm collection/access for a 50k-doc eval?
2) Would you like us to provision a trial MAP (mutual action plan) + demo of the suggested pipeline? We're happy to draft a MAP and an SOW.
3) Rishi/Vivek from my team will provide a short technical note on similarity thresholds and monitoring hooks.

Happy to hop on another sync next week.

Best,

Jordan quick technical supplements to Marissa's note:

Retrieval & reranker practicals:
- Candidate pool sizing: 200-500 is reasonable for 30M doc corpus; start at 200 for latency control and increase if recall suffers.
- Reranker latency: DistilCross-768 typically adds ~25-45ms per request at p95 when running on optimized infra; large cross-encoders will add more. Budget for that in your latency SLOs.
- Similarity thresholds: use a calibrated validation set to pick threshold. In our sample, a post-rerank threshold of 0.45 yielded precision@1 ~0.61 and MRR ~0.58.

Grounding metrics to track (we recommend implementing these in the eval harness):
- Precision@1 (how often top answer is grounded)
- MRR (mean reciprocal rank)
- Hallucination rate (human-labeled share of answers flagged as unsupported)
- Grounding confidence vs answer correctness curve (for fallbacks/escalation)

Quality/regression guardrails:
- Run regression evals whenever you change quantization, distillation, or kernel-level optimizations. We saw a ~2% drop in precision@1 moving to an 8-bit quantized generator in one of our runs; not catastrophic but visible on legal prompts.
- Suggested monitoring: daily eval on a small heldout prompt set (100 prompts) + weekly full eval (2k prompts) with alerting on >3% delta in precision@1 or MRR.

Operational notes:
- For production pilots, enable prefix/KV caching and dynamic batching; these reduce cost without affecting grounding if reranker operates post-retrieval.
- If you need deterministic grounding for compliance, consider a hybrid approach: small generator with template scaffolding + cross-encoder confirmation.

I attached the quick spreadsheet with reranker latency/throughput numbers (reranker_options.xlsx) and linked the bench in Marissa's note. Happy to run a short POC to measure your corpus-specific numbers.

Vivek
